title: Bananas Are Berries, But Strawberries Are Not
short_teaser: The way we name fruits is not always how science classifies them.
story: Botanically speaking, bananas meet the scientific definition of a berry. Strawberries do not because their structure develops differently. The way we name fruits is not always how science classifies them. Curiosity changes an ordinary fact into an invitation. Instead of stopping at what happened, it asks what else might be true, what assumptions may be incomplete, and what becomes visible when we look again. The lasting importance is simple: sometimes what we assume is true is worth exploring. Looking closer can reveal something unexpected.
impact: Sometimes what we assume is true is worth exploring. Looking closer can reveal something unexpected. Curiosity loosens the grip of assumptions and creates room for better questions. This matters because the lesson is transferable. It can help someone recognize a pattern, make a more thoughtful choice, or see possibility where they previously saw only a problem.
spark_application: What assumption in your life or business might be worth questioning? Write three questions about something you have been assuming is fixed. Choose the question that opens the most possibility. Afterward, save a short note about what you noticed, what surprised you, or what you may want to revisit.
